statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk of 17% sits in the low band, below the 20% watch threshold and well below the 25% block level.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold. The retracement off the record high has deepened to roughly 0.34% while the gap above the prior record close stays unfilled, and VIX and the 10-year yield are both easing toward session lows, so conditions read as an orderly uptrend in which mean reversion is demonstrably working. The narrow danger window is limited to the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close.
headline: Nasdaq-100 sets a fresh record then retraces 0.34% with volatility decaying; Tail eases to 17% in the low band
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades at 31,256 (+0.58%) in the US afternoon after printing a fresh record high of 31,361, which is also the new 52-week high. The session range is 31,208-31,361 and price has now retraced about 0.34% from the high, deepening the 0.23% pullback observed an hour earlier. The gap above Monday's 31,076 record close remains unfilled because the session low held 0.42% above it, so the uptrend is intact while retracements are clearly being granted. Cross-asset evidence is supportive rather than amplifying: VIX is 15.14 (-2.45%) and trading near its 14.96 session low, the 10-year yield has eased three basis points to 5.28% near its 5.26 day low as the recent surge pauses, and the 30-year sits around 5.63%. Leadership is narrow, with the Russell 2000 down 0.38% against the Nasdaq-100's gain and the three largest S&P 500 constituents now exceeding 21% of that index, while semiconductors and AI infrastructure names lead the advance. Oil is the main background constraint, with WTI near $89.81 against live Middle East supply risk and a G7 emergency reserve release. Observed deepening retracement, decaying implied volatility and an easing long end together argue against a pathological no-retracement path, so Tail returns to the low band at 17% while Stress stays elevated at 47% on high absolute yields, narrow breadth, index concentration and the oil backdrop. The shared Finviz context file was stale and only partially collected, so this assessment rests entirely on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 hours from 17:00Z on 05 October to 16:00Z on 06 October are covered by published Claude assessments. Tail ran 8-22%: a WATCH print at 19:00Z on 05 October, then compression to 8-12% through the Asian and European overnight, followed by a steady climb from 13% at 10:00Z as the European and US sessions built the gap-up trend. Tail reached 19% at 14:00Z, peaked at a 22% WATCH print at 15:00Z while price was holding within 0.05% of the session high, then eased to 20% at 16:00Z as the first genuine retracement appeared. Stress held in a narrow 45-54% elevated range throughout and Confidence stayed at 86-88%.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band for the remainder of the US afternoon, rising to 20% only for the 19:00Z power hour into the cash close, which is the single narrow danger window. It then steps down through the post-close hours into the low teens and reaches a 10% trough across the Asian session, rebuilding gradually through the European morning to 16% at 12:00Z and 18% for the slot containing the 07 October cash open. The final hours hold 18-19% around the EIA crude inventories at 14:30Z and Consumer Inflation Expectations at 15:00Z. Stress eases from 47-48% to the low 40s overnight before returning to the elevated band for the next US session, and Confidence decays from 87% to 78% with distance from the verified evidence cutoff. Every slot beyond the current clock-hour frames price-path structure conditionally; the FOMC minutes at 18:00Z on 07 October sit just beyond this horizon.
